title: clicky-ui JsonSchemaForm schema
description:
A JSON Schema 2020-12 document annotated for @flanksource/clicky-ui's JsonSchemaForm. It is the standard 2020-12 meta-schema plus the `x-*` presentation keywords the form reads, applied at every depth (nested `properties`, `items`, `allOf` branches, map value schemas). Set `$schema` to this document's `$id` to validate a form schema and get hover documentation in editors.

Control resolution is first-match-wins on schema keywords, never on field names: `x-clicky-lookup` → `enum` (or an `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch carrying an `enum`) → `format: date|date-time` → `format: textarea` → `format: md` → `boolean` → `integer`/`number` → `array` → open string map (`additionalProperties`/`patternProperties`/`propertyNames`) → nested object (`properties`) → string.

Unknown `x-*` keys are allowed: consumers read their own extension keys from `PreExtension`/`PostExtension` functions and the form passes them through untouched.

title.description: The field label. A missing title falls back to the property key; an explicit empty string renders no label at all (for a field whose host already names it).

description.description: Helper text for the field, shown under the control or behind a `?` beside the label (see `x-help-display`). Combined with `x-help.body` when both are present and differ.

default.description: Seeds the value of a field that has none, and is the value an `x-on-change` `reset` action restores (the key is removed when there is no default).

enum.description: Renders the field as a picker over these values. Label, icon, description and tone per value come from `x-enum-labels`, `x-enum-icons`, `x-enum-descriptions` and `x-enum-tones`; the presentation from `x-enum-display`. On `propertyNames`, restricts a map's keys to a picker. On an array's `items`, renders a tag list (or `x-array-display: filter-pills`).

format.description: Standard string format. Formats with form-specific meaning: `date` and `date-time` render a date picker; `textarea` a multi-line text box; `md` the MDXEditor-backed markdown editor (options in `x-md-editor`); `percent` (on a number) shows a static `%` unit inside the input; `password` masks the input and excludes the field from text filtering. Any other format renders a plain string input.

readOnly.description: Renders the field as a read-only value display (no input), or drops it entirely when the form sets `hideReadOnlyFields`. Contrast `x-disabled`, which keeps the real control and disables it. On an object, array or map, the subtree becomes a view, as under a read-only form: its fields keep disabled controls, its tables show values, and its `writeOnly` fields are omitted. In an `x-layout: table` array every cell of a read-only table (the array's own `readOnly`, a `readOnly` ancestor, or a read-only form) renders the same value display as a `readOnly` column; a `readOnly` column is dropped, header and all, under `hideReadOnlyFields`, and a `writeOnly` column is dropped from a read-only table.

maximum.description: Upper bound of a number field. Required for `x-number-display: slider`.

multipleOf.description: Its presence opts a number field into a native `<input type="number">` (with step/min/max) instead of the token-friendly text input.

minItems.description: The form stops offering per-item "remove" at this length. Not validation: an array already outside its bounds is left alone rather than trapped.

maxItems.description: The form stops offering "add" at this length. Not validation: an array already outside its bounds is left alone rather than trapped.

additionalProperties.description: `false` closes the object; `true` opens it as a free string map; a subschema types every extra entry's value (a typed map).

patternProperties.description: Per-key-pattern value schemas for a map: the first regex matching an entry's key types that entry's value, falling back to `additionalProperties`. Lets a keyed map render a different value form per key.

propertyNames.description: An `enum` here turns a map's key input into a picker limited to those keys (labelled from `propertyNames.title`, options labelled by `x-enum-labels`).

allOf.description: Each member is either an `if`/`then`/`else` conditional — the matched branch's `properties`/`required` are merged into the object against the current value, replacing a property wholesale — or an unconditional composition member (a flattened `$ref`) whose `properties`/`required` always merge. An `if` the form cannot evaluate fails closed to `else`.

anyOf.description: Not validated, but mined: a branch carrying an `enum` renders the field as a dropdown (a value-or-template union), and a two-branch union of a string `pattern` plus a number/integer/boolean/date branch renders the native control of the non-template branch.

oneOf.description: Not validated, but mined like `anyOf`: a branch carrying an `enum` renders the field as a dropdown.

x-order.description: Object-level. Property render order: listed keys render first, in this order; unlisted keys keep document order after them. Lets producers whose serializer alphabetizes maps (e.g. Go) state the intended order. For order that composes across merged `allOf` branches use the per-field `x-clicky-order`.

x-clicky-order.description: Field-level render order: lower values sort first; properties without it keep document order after the ordered ones. Unlike `x-order`, it composes across merged `allOf`/`then` branches because each field carries its own rank.

x-hidden.description: Render nothing for this property — no label, no control, at any depth (a hidden object takes its whole section with it). The value is untouched: hiding is a presentation decision, not a data one. Flippable by an `allOf` branch (a matching branch replaces the property wholesale, so re-declare it with `"x-hidden": false` to reveal it) or by an `x-on-change` `show`/`hide` action or `patch`.

x-disabled.description: Render the field's real control, disabled (containers disable their whole subtree). Unlike `readOnly`, which swaps the input for plain value text. Flippable by an `allOf` branch like `x-hidden`, and set/cleared by an `x-on-change` `enable`/`disable` action or `patch`.

x-on-change.description: Change listeners on this field. Each entry's actions target SIBLING keys of the object that declares this property, applying while `when` holds (always, when `when` is omitted) and `else` applying while it does not. A `hide`/`show`/`enable`/`disable` target or a `patch` key may instead be a `/`-separated path into a sibling's subtree (`groups/Rates/Amount`): each later segment names a property of the object reached so far, and an array is crossed into its `items` without spending a segment. State actions (`hide`/`show`, `enable`/`disable`, `require`/`optional`, `patch`) are derived: re-evaluated from the current value on every render, so a reloaded record shows the shape it was saved with. Value actions (`reset`/`set`) are transitional: they fire only when this field is committed through the form, and cascade into the listeners of the fields they change (each key fires at most once per commit). `require`/`optional`/`reset`/`set` take sibling keys only, never a path. Listeners apply in order after the object's `x-on-load`, a later one winning per target.

x-on-load.description: Object-level load listeners: the state the object's properties start in. Applied before any property's `x-on-change`, in order: the object's own, then each `allOf` member's — an unconditional member's own, or those of the `then`/`else` branch that currently applies. `when` is evaluated against the object itself (a nested `properties` predicate reads its fields; `expr` gets `key: ""` and the object as `value` and `self`). Only derived state is allowed — `hide`/`show`, `enable`/`disable` and `patch`, with the same path targets as `x-on-change`; `set`, `reset`, `require` and `optional` are refused.

x-icon.description: Leading glyph for the field label: a runtime icon name resolved by the form's icon provider.

x-help.description: Inline help metadata emitted by CLI/schema generators. `body` is rendered together with `description` as the field's helper text.

x-help-display.description: How this field's description is presented, overriding the form-level `layout.help`. `inline` is a paragraph under the control; `hover` moves it behind a `?` beside the label.

x-label-position.description: Friendlier alias for the per-field layout: `top` stacks the label above the value (`x-layout: stack`); `left` places it beside the value (`x-layout: inline`). `x-layout` wins when both are set.

x-label-classes.description: Extra CSS classes merged onto the field's `<label>`. Tailwind classes only compile if the consumer's Tailwind build scans a file containing them.

x-input-classes.description: Extra CSS classes merged onto the field's input element. Tailwind classes only compile if the consumer's Tailwind build scans a file containing them.

x-input-prefix.description: Static text rendered inside the input at its left edge (display only, never part of the value). `x-input-prefix-icon` wins when both are set.

x-input-suffix.description: Static text rendered inside the input at its right edge (display only, never part of the value). `x-input-suffix-icon` wins when both are set.

x-input-prefix-icon.description: Runtime icon name rendered inside the input at its left edge. Wins over `x-input-prefix`.

x-input-suffix-icon.description: Runtime icon name rendered inside the input at its right edge. Wins over `x-input-suffix`.

x-layout.description: Per-field layout override, taking precedence over the form-level layout. `inline` and `stack` force the field's subtree into label-beside-value or label-above-value mode; `table` renders an array of objects (or a map) as compact rows under column headers. On a map's value schema, `stack` renders each key above its value as one full-width unit.

x-columns.description: Object-level. Lay the object's fields out in N equal columns (stacked layout); fields span one column unless they set `x-col-span`. `auto` fits as many equal columns as the container width allows, each at least `x-column-min-width` wide.

x-column-min-width.description: Object-level, with `x-columns: auto` only. Minimum width of one column as a CSS length (default `15rem`). A length rather than a class, because a class inside a schema is data no Tailwind scanner ever reads.

x-columns-max-width.description: Object-level, with `x-columns: auto` only. Optional cap on the whole grid's width, as a CSS length.

x-col-span.description: How many of the enclosing object's columns this field occupies (honoured when the object sets `x-columns`). `full` spans the whole row — the only meaningful answer under `x-columns: auto` — and lifts the stacked value-width cap.

x-classes.description: Object-level. Extra CSS classes merged onto the object's fields-grid container, e.g. `gap-2` for the section's row/column gap.

x-enum-labels.description: Human label per enum value. The option renders as `Label (value)` while the raw value is what is stored. Also applies to `propertyNames.enum` key pickers.

x-enum-icons.description: Runtime icon name per enum value. Its presence switches the enum control to a selectable icon grid unless `x-enum-display` says otherwise; `x-item.glyph` and `x-item.badge` also read it.

x-enum-descriptions.description: Secondary descriptive line per enum value, rendered by the `segmented` (as descriptive cards) and `grid` displays.

x-enum-tones.description: Hue per enum value. Purely decorative — unlike `x-enum-icons` it does not change which enum control renders. Read by displays that colour a value, e.g. the accordion array's leading glyph (`x-item.glyph`).

x-enum-display.description: Force the enum presentation. `combobox` (the default) is a searchable dropdown; `radio` a segmented radio group for small fixed sets; `grid` a filterable grid of icon cards (the default when `x-enum-icons` is present); `segmented` the shared SegmentedControl, rendering large descriptive cards when `x-enum-descriptions` is present.

x-array-display.description: Force an array's presentation. `filter-pills` renders each enum item option as a compact toggle (an empty array means all options); `accordion` (the default for object items) collapses each item to a summary row and opens one at a time; `cards` keeps every item open under a titled header; both read `x-item`. `stacked` opts out to one full sub-form per item labelled *Item N*; `list` renders scalar values as compact editable list items.

x-item.description: Array-level. How to summarize one item in a collapsed accordion row or card header. Every value names a property of the item. Lives on the array rather than on `items` because one shared item schema may be summarized differently by each array that uses it.

x-number-display.description: Render a bounded number (requires `maximum`) as a single-thumb slider with a progress-filled track instead of a numeric input.

x-discriminator.description: Object-level. Names the property whose value selects a "kind" (e.g. a connection `type`). The form renders that property first as a picker; once chosen, it shows the matched `allOf` branch's fields and collapses the picker to a compact header with a "change" affordance.

x-md-editor.description: Options for the MDXEditor-backed markdown field rendered for `format: md`. Only the JSON-serializable subset of `MdxEditorPluginOptions` can be declared in a schema; function-valued options (image upload/preview handlers, `jsxComponents`, `plugins`, code block `editorDescriptors`, toolbar `extra`) must be supplied programmatically.

x-clicky-lookup.description: Turns the field into an async entity-reference picker: options are fetched lazily from another entity's list endpoint via the form's `lookupFetcher`. Single-select also accepts free-form entry; set `multi` for an array field.

x-clicky-unit.description: Opt-in: honoured only when the consumer passes `createUnitFormExtensions()` to the form. Renders a positive integer as a unit-scaled input with step controls — `count` (K/M/B/T) or `bytes` (KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB).

x-clicky-component.description: Opt-in: honoured only when the consumer passes `createSecretFormExtensions(...)` to the form. Replaces the control with a Kubernetes value-source selector — `k8s-secret-selector` for a secret/configmap/value reference, `k8s-url-selector` for the same plus a workload endpoint.

x-clicky-default-source.description: Opt-in, with `x-clicky-component`. The source a new, empty secret reference starts on.

FieldTone.description: The closed palette of decorative hues. Each tone tracks the light/dark theme.

source.description: Where the help text came from (e.g. a CLI command).

section.description: The section of the source it was taken from.

body.description: Help text, appended to `description` in the rendered helper text.

examples.body: Must be unique within the namespace.

ChangeActionTargets.description: Sibling property keys the action applies to. `hide`/`show`/`enable`/`disable` also accept a `/`-separated path into a sibling's subtree; the other actions take keys only.

hide.description: Derived: hide these siblings while the condition holds.

show.description: Derived: show these siblings (clearing `x-hidden`) while the condition holds.

enable.description: Derived: enable these siblings (clearing `x-disabled`) while the condition holds.

disable.description: Derived: disable these siblings while the condition holds.

require.description: Derived: mark these siblings required while the condition holds.

optional.description: Derived: mark these siblings optional while the condition holds.

reset.description: Transitional: on commit, restore these siblings to their schema `default`, or remove them when they have none.

set.description: Transitional: on commit, set each sibling key to the literal value given.

patch.description: Derived: per sibling key (or `/`-separated path into a sibling's subtree), keywords shallow-merged over that property while the condition holds — `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `title`, `description`, `enum`, bounds, any presentation `x-*`. Applied after the other state actions; a later listener wins per keyword. A patch may not set a keyword a hide/show or enable/disable in the same actions also sets.

ChangePatch.description: Keywords merged over one sibling property. Refused: keywords that change the property's shape (use an `allOf` branch), `required` (use `require`/`optional`), value keywords `default`/`const` (use `set`/`reset`), and the listener keywords `x-on-change`/`x-on-load`.

ChangeListener.description: One `x-on-change` entry: its actions apply while `when` holds (always, when omitted), and `else` applies while it does not.

when.description: Condition on THIS field's value, in the `if`-predicate grammar the form evaluates (`const`, `enum`, `not`, nested `properties`/`required`), plus an optional `expr` handed to the form's `expressionEvaluator`. When both are present both must hold. A condition with nothing evaluable is an error.

expr.description: Expression evaluated by the host's `expressionEvaluator`; must return a boolean.

else.description: Actions applied while `when` does not hold.

LoadActionNames.description: Actions an `x-on-load` entry may not use: load state is derived, never a value or required-ness change.

LoadListener.description: One `x-on-load` entry: a ChangeListener whose `when` reads the object itself, limited to `hide`/`show`, `enable`/`disable` and `patch`.

property.description: Item property whose value is shown.

pattern.description: Wraps the value; a single literal `{}` marks where it goes.

title.description: Item property keys tried in order; the first with a non-empty value is the row title.

fallback.description: Title used when every `title` candidate is empty. Defaults to `Item <n>`.

summary.description: The monospace trailing line, parts joined with " · ". A string names an item property; an object wraps it in a `pattern`.

glyph.description: Enum item property supplying the leading glyph's icon (`x-enum-icons`) and tone (`x-enum-tones`).

badge.description: Enum item property supplying a secondary chip.

flag.description: Boolean item property rendered as the required mark.

actions.description: Which per-item actions rows offer. Omit for all of them; `[]` for none. `reorder` covers both the up and the down button.

noun.description: Noun for the add row ("Add parameter"). Defaults to `items.title`, then "item".

nounPlural.description: Plural for the count line ("4 parameters"). Defaults to the array title, then "items".

empty.description: Copy shown by the add row at zero items. Defaults to the array's own description.

url.description: Entity list path that serves the lookup.

filter.description: Filter key sent as `__lookup_filter`; the response keys its options (and the committed value) under it.

searchParam.description: Query-string key for the search term. Informational — the client always sends `__lookup_q`.

multi.description: Allow multiple selected values (for an array field). Single-select also accepts free-form entry.

scope.description: Derive an extra query param from another field so the option set is filtered by it.

from.description: Dotted path into the form's root value.

map.description: Maps the source value to the emitted values. When absent the source value is sent verbatim.

join.description: Joins mapped values into the param. Defaults to ",".

hierarchy.description: Render options as a browsable tree by splitting each label on any character in `delimiters`. Presentational only — the committed value is the unsplit option value.

delimiters.description: Characters separating one level from the next.

toolbar.description: Show the toolbar, optionally positioned and styled.

headings.description: Enable headings, optionally limited to some levels.

languages.description: Language id → display name, or a list of language descriptors.

callouts.description: Register `<CalloutBox>` with its own node editor. Off by default.

source.description: Module the component is imported from, if the document needs the import.

diffMode.description: Enable the rich-text/source/diff view switcher, or start in a given view mode.

diffMarkdown.description: Baseline markdown the diff view compares against.
